page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.8-32 is a general-purpose compute instance built on the Ampere Altra processor architecture. This configuration supplies 8 dedicated 64-bit Arm (arm64) physical cores running at a fixed 3.0 GHz frequency with a single thread per core, mapping directly to 8 vCPUs. The compute allotment is paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core.

The instance operates without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs and no local NVMe disks. Data persistence relies entirely on remote cloud block storage solutions. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. By utilizing dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, the architecture avoids core-sharing contention, ensuring stable performance across execution cycles.

Arm-based hardware profiles offer favorable operational cost efficiency through power-efficient scaling and predictable execution metrics across multi-core systems. The principal tradeoff rests on software architecture requirements, necessitating that applications and operational toolchains are compiled for the 64-bit Arm instruction set.

VM.Standard.A1.Flex.8-32 is matched to balanced enterprise workloads suited for AArch64 platforms, including containerized microservices, middle-tier API services, static and dynamic web application serving, development environments, and distributed build pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A1.Flex.8-32 is an arm64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by Ampere Altra processors. It features 8 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.0 GHz with a single-threaded configuration (1 thread per core), equating to 8 vCPUs. The instance contains 32.0 GB of memory, delivering a balanced 4.0 GB per core distribution suitable for diverse computing tasks. There are zero GPU accelerators and no bundled local storage disks, necessitating external network-attached storage for stateful data. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Because the platform assigns dedicated physical Arm cores rather than shared hyperthreads, workloads benefit from predictable thread performance without resource contention. This architecture delivers efficient computing capacity for software compatible with the AArch64 ecosystem. The instance is designed for web serving, microservice orchestration, development build systems, and general business applications.
